t: This is the Lyric Theatre, a West End house on Shaftesbury Avenue. It was built for the producer Henry Leslie, who paid for it with the profits of a light opera hit called Dorothy, which he moved from its first venue to open this one on 17 December 1888. The architect was Charles J. Phipps, who designed more than forty theatres in the second half of the nineteenth century. So this is one of many Phipps theatres, and it is still working as a theatre today.
